text: This quartier contains the Eiffel Tower and Champ de Mars, and is the one part of the 7th arrondissement with well-documented, recurring problems. By day, French press and police have repeatedly covered organised illegal souvenir vendors clashing with police and targeting/pickpocketing tourists around the tower, prompting a major municipal police operation with over 100 officers in August 2025 and prior crackdown efforts ahead of the 2024 Olympics. More seriously, French outlets reported sexual assaults on tourists at the Champ de Mars at night, serious enough that right-wing city councillors publicly called for the park to be closed after dark and security around the monument was questioned ahead of the Olympics. Extra caution after dark in this specific park area is warranted; the tower itself and surrounding streets by day are heavily patrolled.
sources: franceinfo, 2023 (report ahead of Paris 2024 on street vendors)
policeetrealites.com, August 2025 (police operation vs. illegal vendors)
ici/France Bleu, 2023 ("soupçons de viol sur le Champ-de-Mars", calls to close the park at night)
Fox News, 2023 ("Eiffel Tower crime wave")

text: The avenue itself is heavily patrolled and generally fine to walk by day, but it is a genuine, recurring flashpoint. A luxury jewellery store just off the avenue was robbed in May 2024 (CNEWS, franceinfo), and the avenue has repeatedly been the epicentre of serious crowd violence tied to major events: the 2025 PSG Champions League celebrations turned into deadly riots with two deaths and hundreds of arrests nationally, centred on the Champs-Élysées, and similar large-scale disorder recurred there after a 2026 PSG-Arsenal match. Every New Year's Eve the Prefecture deploys thousands of officers specifically because of the avenue's known disorder risk. Travellers should be cautious here at night, especially around major football finals, New Year's Eve, or other mass celebrations.
sources: CNEWS, 18 May 2024 (jewellery store robbery)
Wikipedia/AP coverage via Al Jazeera, Euronews, NPR, June 2025 (PSG celebration riots)
fdesouche.com, June 2026 (repeat post-match riots)
CNEWS, December 2025 (New Year's Eve security deployment)

text: This quartier is essentially the Gare du Nord/Lariboisière area, and it is genuinely one of the most consistently documented problem zones in central Paris: it sits inside an official police 'zone de sécurité prioritaire' (bounded by boulevard de la Chapelle, rue La Fayette, boulevard de Magenta and rue Philippe-de-Girard), and press and resident accounts describe open crack use and dealing, syringes on the pavement and frequent assaults around the station. A knife attack injured six to seven people here in January 2023, though the attacker was later found to have been in psychiatric crisis rather than acting for gain — travellers should treat the area as a legitimate no-lingering zone after dark, with daytime risk mainly pickpocketing/petty theft given the huge passenger volume.

franceinfo, 'Attaque à l'arme blanche qui a fait six blessés à la gare du Nord', 11 Jan 2023

text: This quartier covers Boulevard de Strasbourg and rue du Château-d'Eau, where a prefectural order (issued December 2024, extended through May 2026) forces many shops — largely Afro-Caribbean hair salons — to close between 8pm and 5am, and bans off-premises alcohol sales overnight, citing 'repeated disturbances to public order,' unauthorised street occupation and unlicensed vending. The measure is genuinely controversial (Paris Council rejected a motion against it in October 2025, with critics saying it stigmatises the businesses rather than fixing the underlying disorder), but its existence confirms real, official-level nighttime nuisance concerns in this exact strip. Daytime is mostly just crowded and commercial.
sources: Mairie du 10e, 'Arrêté préfectoral: les commerces fermés dès 20h à Château d'Eau', Dec 2024
Groupe Écologiste de Paris, council motion on the closure order, Oct 2025

This quartier includes Place Henri-Frenay, immediately beside Gare de Lyon, which is a genuinely well-documented, recurring problem spot: residents describe daily open drug dealing, people sleeping rough on mattresses, public defecation and regular nighttime fights and screaming, and a family reported witnessing a shooting on nearby rue Roland-Barthes (recovered shell casings) roughly in 2022. A man attacked three people with a knife at Gare de Lyon on 4 February 2024 (one victim critically injured). As of an August 2025 city update, the square was still receiving 'exceptional' cleaning and coordinated police resources pending a redevelopment plan, meaning the disorder was still current more than a year after the attack. Daytime is visibly rougher than the surrounding area but not violent in the same way; after dark this specific corner (not the whole quartier) is best avoided.

Porte de la Chapelle itself has also repeatedly hosted large open-air drug-user encampments (the so-called "colline du crack"), evacuated by police multiple times between 2019 and 2024 and re-forming nearby each time. Real, well-documented risk exists here both day and night, worse after dark.

text: Most of this quartier — Parc de la Villette, Cité des Sciences, the Philharmonie — is a large, family-friendly public park and is not itself a documented trouble spot. But its northern edge at Porte de la Villette/Square Forceval has repeatedly hosted large open-air crack-use encampments: a 1,000-officer police operation dismantled one there in October 2022 (Le Journal du Grand Paris), and users have cyclically returned to nearby dealing points since, per ongoing tracking of the "colline du crack" phenomenon. Stick to the main park/museum areas and avoid the Porte de la Villette perimeter, especially at night.
sources: Le Journal du Grand Paris, 5 Oct 2022

text: This quartier includes the Avenue de Flandre/Stalingrad-Riquet canal corridor, one of the most persistently documented open-air crack-dealing zones in Paris: Sortiraparis described dealers arriving predictably around 6pm and running an "Uber Eats du crack"-style operation concentrated on just a few streets under residents' windows, and this Stalingrad-area problem was still being cited as an active concern in December 2025 press coverage (Europe1). The Bassin de la Villette waterfront itself is popular and generally fine by day; the Riquet-Stalingrad blocks are best avoided, especially after dark.
